newsitem.title: INDIA: India sets up panel on sugarcane productivity.
newsitem.headline: India sets up panel on sugarcane productivity.

text.p: The Indian government has set up a high powered committee to suggest ways to increase sugarcane productivity and review sugar industry laws, a Food Ministry statement said on Friday.
The committee will also look at ways to ensure a fair price for sugarcane growers.

"The terms of reference of the committee include study of laws and regulations relating to sugar, sugarcane and sugar industry in India and other sugar producing countries and to suggest methods for increase in productivity of sugarcane," the statement said.
Sugar supplies and pricing in India are controlled by the government.
The mills supply 40 percent of the output as levy at a subsidised rate for distribution among the poor and sell the balance in the open market, regulated over a period of 12 months.

India began abolishing licenses for many industries under a reform programme that began in 1991, but it kept sugar under the old regime which has subsidised prices for consumers and protected producers.
The committee, to be headed by B.B. Mahajan, a retired food ministry official, will submit its report to the government within six months. -- New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
